# kifbetadiversity

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/OdedHol/kifbetadiversity/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/OdedHol/kifbetadiversity/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

You sampled two habitats and want to know which one is more heterogeneous.
The sites in one habitat may look more alike than those in the other, but is
that difference real, or just sampling noise?

kifbetadiversity estimates Whittaker's multiplicative beta diversity
(`beta_M = gamma / alpha - 1`) with a confidence interval, and tests whether
two habitats differ, following Kiflawi & Spencer (2004, *Ecology*
85(10):2895-2900). Regional richness (gamma) is estimated with the
first-order jackknife, so the result accounts for species your survey missed
and for the uncertainty in gamma.

## Installation

In RStudio, run:

``` r
install.packages("remotes")   # first time only
remotes::install_github("OdedHol/kifbetadiversity", build_vignettes = TRUE)
library(kifbetadiversity)
```

On Windows, if R asks to install Rtools, you can answer no: the package has
no compiled code.

## Which shape is your data?

Field data usually comes in one of two shapes. Pick the matching function
to prepare it; after that, both paths are the same.

**Shape 1: one row per record** (each row is one species found at one site)

```
site     species  habitat  count
open_01  sp04     open     3
open_01  sp10     open     2
tree_01  sp05     tree     3
```

```r
res <- as_site_by_species(records, site = "site", species = "species",
                          value = "count", group = "habitat",
                          all_sites = sites)   # every site surveyed, incl. empty ones
```

**Shape 2: one row per site, one column per species** (often with extra
columns such as an ID, a habitat or a richness total)

```
plot_num  habitat  site_id  richness  sp01  sp02  sp03  ...
1         open     open_01  6         0     0     0     ...
1         tree     tree_01  7         0     0     0     ...
```

```r
res <- as_site_table(tab, site = "site_id", group = "habitat",
                     species = "sp01:sp45")   # only the species columns
```

Every column you give as `species` counts as a species, so leave out IDs
and totals like `plot_num` and `richness`. The site column must be unique
per row: `plot_num` repeats across habitats, so `site_id` is used.

**Then, for both shapes:**

```r
beta_diversity(res$x, group = res$group)        # beta and its 95% CI per habitat
beta_diversity_test(res$x, group = res$group)   # do the two habitats differ?
```

## A full example

The package includes a small made-up survey (30 open and 30 tree sites) in
both shapes. Replace the file paths with your own CSV.

```{r example}
library(kifbetadiversity)

tab <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "example_site_table.csv",
                            package = "kifbetadiversity"))
res <- as_site_table(tab, site = "site_id", group = "habitat",
                     species = "sp01:sp45")

beta_diversity(res$x, group = res$group)
beta_diversity_test(res$x, group = res$group)
```

`beta_M` is Whittaker's beta as in Kiflawi & Spencer (2004),
`gamma_hat / alpha - 1`. `beta_W` is the conventional `gamma_hat / alpha`,
which is simply `beta_M + 1`. Both carry the same information, and the test
is the same for either.

To read your own file, use `tab <- read.csv(file.choose())` and change the
column names to match. The vignette explains every column, the assumptions
behind the test (sites must be independent and comparably sampled) and
common errors:

``` r
vignette("kifbetadiversity")
```

## Citation

If you use kifbetadiversity, please cite the method it implements:

> Kiflawi, M., & Spencer, M. (2004). Confidence intervals and hypothesis
> testing for beta diversity. *Ecology*, 85(10), 2895-2900.
